unit.why: A short anecdote about Rabbi Zvi (of Zhidachov), passed down through a chain of tellers. He hears a heavenly proclamation honouring him after prayer in tallit and tefillin, then a proclamation of woe after he moves an object without the unification of God's name.
unit.boundary_note: Part of a numbered series of short items from the same source; the next item (יח) is a related saying, not a continuation.

stories.summary_en: After praying in tallit and tefillin, R. Zvi heard a heavenly call to honour the King's image. At home he forgot himself and moved an object without the unification of God's name, and heard a call of woe on one who rebels against his Master.

quotes: שמע שמכריזין למעלה הבו יקר לדיוקנא דמלכא

tags.why: He wears tallit and tefillin; the 'King's image' praise is tied to them.
He walks home from the study hall.
Contemplative unification of the Name before each action.
Unification of the divine Name as a devotional act; borderline.
The closing comment evokes awe and trembling.
Heavenly rebuke for a lapse; borderline, since no actual punishment follows.
Supernatural disclosure of the heavenly verdict.

quotes: ששמע מהרה״ק ר׳ שלמה מדאלינא ז"ל ששמע מרבינו צבי
